profiles.welcome: Learn to code by building your own game!

home.basicsIntro: Learn the building blocks of code with Bit the robot.
home.gamesIntro: Pick a game and build it step by step.

lesson.useArrows: Use the arrow keys on your keyboard!
lesson.clickSquaresFlags: Click the squares! Right-click to place a flag.
lesson.buildFences: Click the lawn to build! Right-click for a fence.

msg.gameDoneSub: You made a real game with code. Well done!
msg.noStart: Put your blocks inside "when Run is clicked".
msg.noKeys: Add "when key … is pressed" blocks so you can steer.
msg.bump: Ouch! Bit bumped into a wall.
msg.notAtFlag: Not quite! Bit stopped before the flag.
msg.coinsLeft: Almost! {n} coin(s) are still lying there.
msg.scoreWrong: The score is {score}, but it should be {want}.
msg.loop: Your code ran too many times. Is a repeat block too big?
msg.tooManySteps: Bit walked too many steps and got tired.
msg.gameOverNotWall: Game over, but not by the wall. Try steering into the wall!
msg.gameOverNotSelf: Game over, but the snake did not bite itself. Make it long and turn into itself!
msg.scoreGoal: Game over! You got {score}. Try to get {want} points!
msg.snakeLeft: The snake slithered off the screen!
msg.snakeLeftHint: The snake slithered off the screen! Add a rule: if the snake hits the wall, then game over.
msg.noFood: Tip: use "place food" so the snake has something to eat.
msg.noStartCode: Put your code inside function whenRunClicked() { … }
msg.noKeysCode: Write functions like whenKeyUp() { … } so you can steer.
msg.badDirection: "{dir}" is not a direction. Use 'up', 'down', 'left' or 'right'.
msg.badColour: "{colour}" is not a snake colour. Pick one of: {list}.
msg.loopCode: A loop ran far too many times, maybe forever. Check the condition of your loop.
msg.offField: There is no square at column {x}, row {y}. Columns go from 0 to {maxX}, and rows from 0 to {maxY}.
msg.badNumber: "{n}" is not a number of mines. Show a whole number like 0, 1 or 2.
msg.tooDeep: The squares kept clicking each other, again and again. Only click around when count is 0.
msg.noClick: Put your blocks inside "when a square is clicked".
msg.noClickCode: Write function whenSquareClicked(x, y) { … } so clicks do something.
msg.noMines: Tip: use "place 10 mines" when the game starts, or the field is empty. Click the squares!
msg.wrongNumber: Column {x}, row {y} shows {shown}, but the right number is {real}. Check your counting!
msg.boom: Boom! You opened a mine. Press Run to play again.
msg.mineNoRule: You opened a mine, but the game goes on! Add the rule: if there is a mine, game over.
msg.mineNoRuleYet: That was a mine, but nothing happened. We'll fix that in the next lesson!
msg.wrongNumberLow: Column {x}, row {y} shows {shown}, but the right number is {real}. The count was too low when the square was opened: is count = count + 1 inside the if? And is field.reveal below the loop, after counting is done?
msg.wrongNumberHigh: Column {x}, row {y} shows {shown}, but the right number is {real}. The count was too high: does count start at 0, and do you add 1 only when there is a mine?
msg.badEvery: "{n}" is not a number of ticks. Use a whole number like 10 or 20.
msg.noSprinkler: There is no sprinkler at column {x}, row {y}, so no water can come from there.
msg.coinsNegative: Your coins went below 0! You can only build when you can afford it: check with if (coins ≥ 10) first.
msg.bugsWon: A bug got into the house! Game over. Press Run to try again.
msg.bugInHouseNoRule: A bug got into Bit's house, but the game goes on! Add the rule: if a bug reached the house, game over.
msg.bugInHouseYet: A bug got into Bit's house! We'll add a rule for that in a later lesson.
msg.buildingIsFree: You stopped the bugs, but building was free! Make building cost 10 coins.
msg.badSpeed: "{speed}" is not a speed. Use a number from 0 to {max}, like 0.05.
msg.bugsStandStill: The bugs came, but they stand still. Open the 🐌 Bug tab: every bug should move itself in its "every game tick".
msg.bugsNotOwn: The bugs still use the standard speed and HP. In 🐌 Bug, give them their own in "when I'm created".
msg.hitNothing: Water hits the bugs, but nothing happens. In 🐌 Bug, decide what happens in "when water hits me".
msg.hpGone: A bug has 0 HP (or less), but it is still crawling! Squash it when its HP runs out.
msg.noBugCoins: You stopped the bugs, but they gave no coins. In 🐌 Bug, give 5 coins when a bug is squashed.
msg.badTile: "{tile}" is not something you can put on the map. Use one of: {list}.
msg.noMap: Put your blocks inside "when ▶ Run is clicked" in 🗺️ Map.
msg.noMapCode: Put your map code inside function whenRunClicked() { … } in 🗺️ Map.
msg.mapNotFull: Only {n} of the {all} squares have something on them. Use two loops so every row and every column gets grass.
msg.mapNoExtras: Lovely lawn! Now put at least one rock or some flowers on the map, wherever you like.
msg.notGrass: Sprinklers can only be built on grass. Click a grass square (or give the 🗺️ Map more grass).

help.key: when an arrow key is pressed: whenKeyUp, whenKeyDown, whenKeyLeft, whenKeyRight
help.score: change the score (the number is how much)
help.if: if the question is true, do what is inside { }
help.log: write a message in the box under your code
help.click: when a square is clicked: x is its column, y is its row
help.placeMines: hide mines in the field (the number is how many)
help.reveal: open the square at column x, row y
help.revealN: open the square and show a number on it
help.hasMine: is there a mine at column x, row y? (true or false)
help.hasMineSquare: is there a mine on that square?
help.flag: put a flag on the square, or take it away
help.clickAround: click every closed square around it (runs whenSquareClicked again)
help.neighbours: a loop: visit the 8 squares around, one at a time
help.countSet: make a variable called count, starting at 0
help.countZero: asks: is count the same as 0?
help.build: build a sprinkler on the square
help.buildFence: build a fence on the square
help.every: a timer: true once every 30 ticks (change the number)
help.coinsEnough: asks: do you have at least 10 coins?
help.stoppedEnough: asks: have you stopped at least 15 bugs?
help.created: runs once, when this object is created
help.hit: runs when water hits this bug
help.meMove: move this bug forward (with its own speed)
help.meHp: this bug's HP: how much it can take
help.meChangeHp: take 1 HP away from this bug
help.hpGone: asks: is this bug's HP 0 or less?
help.meSquash: squash this bug: it is stopped
help.meShoot: this sprinkler shoots a drop along its row
help.forRows: a loop over every row: y is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
help.forColumns: a loop over every column: x is 0, 1, … 8

err.string: This text has no closing {q}. Text must start and end with {q}.
err.comment: This /* comment */ is never closed with */.
err.extraClose: There is one {ch} too many here.
err.mismatch: Here is a {close}, but the {open} on line {openLine} needs a {want} first.
err.unclosed: This {open} is never closed. Add a {close} where it should end.
err.loopBraces: Put the code for your "{kw}" loop inside { }.
err.eventName: "{name}" should be written {want}. Capital letters matter!
err.syntax: The computer doesn't understand this line. Check for typos. ({detail})
err.notDefined: "{name}" doesn't exist. Check the spelling: capital letters matter!
err.notFunction: There is no command called {name}. Check the spelling, or look in the command list.
err.recursion: A function calls itself again and again, forever.
err.tooMany: You may use {name} only {max} time(s) here, but you used it {used} times. Use a loop!
err.notInLesson: There is no {name} in this lesson.
err.noCommand: {name} is not a command. Check the spelling, or look in the Commands list for what {obj} can do.
err.wrongCase: {name} should be written {want}. Capital letters matter!
err.needParens: {name} needs ( ) after it, or it won't run: {name}()
err.unusedQuestion: {name}(…) asks a question, but nothing uses the answer, so this line does nothing. Put it inside if ( … ) { } and put what should happen inside the { }.
err.revealInLoop: This opens the square while the loop is still counting, so the number is not finished yet. Move it below the } on line {line}, where the loop ends.
err.commandInIf: {name}(…) is a command, not a question, so it can't be inside the ( ) of {kw}. The ( ) only hold the question. Move the command out: into the { } if it should only happen when the answer is yes, or below the }.
err.twoInIf: There are two things next to each other inside the ( ) of {kw}. The ( ) hold one question. To ask two at once, join them with && (and) or || (or).
err.noMeHere: me only exists in an object's script, like 🐌 Bug or 💧 Sprinkler. In 🏡 Garden there is no "me".
err.propCalled: {name} is a value, not a command, so it has no ( ) after it. Use it like a variable: {name} = 3;

code.symbolsTip: Click on any symbol or word in your code to see what it means there.

warn.semicolon: Put a ; at the end of this command, like a full stop at the end of a sentence.

explain.idle: Click on any symbol or word in your code, and I'll tell you what it means.
explain.comment: // starts a comment: a note for people reading the code. The computer skips everything after // on that line.
explain.string: {text} is text. The quotes ' ' show where the text starts and ends, so the computer knows it's a word to use, not a command.
explain.number: {n} is a number. You can change it.
explain.semicolon: ; ends a command, like a full stop ends a sentence.
explain.semicolonFor: Inside for ( ), the ; splits the three parts: where the counter starts, how long to keep going, and how the counter changes.
explain.brace: { } curly brackets hold a group of code that belongs together.
explain.braceEvent: { } hold the code of {name}. Everything between { and } runs when that happens.
explain.braceFunction: { } hold the code of the function {name}. It runs every time you write {name}().
explain.braceIf: { } hold the code that only runs if the question in if ( ) is true.
explain.braceElse: { } hold the code that runs when the if question is NOT true.
explain.braceLoop: { } hold the code the loop repeats. Everything between { and } runs again each time round.
explain.paren: ( ) round brackets group things together, like in maths.
explain.parenIf: ( ) after if hold a question. The code in { } only runs if the answer is yes (true).
explain.parenFor: ( ) after for hold three parts, split by ; : where the counter starts, how long to keep going, and how the counter changes each time.
explain.parenWhile: ( ) after while hold a question. The loop keeps going as long as the answer is yes (true).
explain.parenFunction: ( ) after {name}: here a function can ask for extra information. Empty ( ) means it needs none.
explain.parenCall: ( ) after {name} make the command run. What's inside is extra information for it, like which way to go.
explain.parenCallEmpty: ( ) after {name} make the command run. It needs no extra information, but you still need the ( ), or it won't run!
explain.dot: The dot means "belongs to". bit.move is the move command that belongs to Bit.
explain.comma: A comma separates things in a list.
explain.assign: = puts a value into a variable. let i = 0 means: make a box called i and put 0 in it. (To ask "are they the same?" you use ===.)
explain.less: < means "less than". i < 4 is true while i is 0, 1, 2 or 3.
explain.greater: > means "more than". score > 5 is true when the score is 6 or more.
explain.lessEq: <= means "less than or the same as".
explain.greaterEq: >= means "more than or the same as".
explain.equals: {op} asks: are these two the same? The answer is true or false.
explain.notEquals: {op} asks: are these two different? The answer is true or false.
explain.plusPlus: ++ adds 1. i++ is a short way to write i = i + 1.
explain.minusMinus: -- takes away 1. i-- is a short way to write i = i - 1.
explain.plus: + adds numbers together (or joins text together).
explain.minus: - takes one number away from another.
explain.remainder: % gives what's left over after dividing: 7 % 3 is 1.
explain.not: ! means "not". It turns true into false, and false into true.
explain.and: && means "and": both sides must be true.
explain.or: || means "or": one side being true is enough.
explain.squareBrackets: [ ] square brackets make a list, or pick one thing out of a list.
explain.plusEquals: += adds to a variable. score += 2 is short for score = score + 2.
explain.minusEquals: -= takes away from a variable. lives -= 1 is short for lives = lives - 1.
explain.arrow: => makes a short function: what comes before it is the input, and after it is what the function does.
explain.colon: : separates a name from its value.
explain.function: function makes a named piece of code. Its code goes between { and }.
explain.for: for is a loop: it repeats the code in { }. The ( ) say how many times.
explain.while: while is a loop: it repeats the code in { } as long as the question in ( ) is true.
explain.do: do starts a loop that runs the code in { } first, and asks the while question after.
explain.if: if lets the code choose: the code in { } only runs if the question in ( ) is true.
explain.else: else means "otherwise": its { } code runs when the if question is not true.
explain.let: let makes a new variable: a box with a name that remembers a value, like a score.
explain.const: const makes a box with a name whose value never changes.
explain.return: return ends the function and gives back a value.
explain.true: true means yes. Questions like bit.isOnCoin() answer true or false.
explain.false: false means no. Questions like bit.isOnCoin() answer true or false.
explain.break: break stops the loop straight away.
explain.continue: continue skips the rest of this time round the loop and starts the next one.
explain.event_start: {name} is a special name: its code runs once, when you press ▶ Run. Capital letters matter!
explain.event_tick: {name} is a special name: its code runs again and again, many times every second, while the game is on.
explain.event_key: {name} is a special name: its code runs every time the {key} arrow key is pressed.
explain.bit: bit is Bit the robot. Write a dot after it to use one of Bit's commands, like bit.move.
explain.snake: snake is your snake. Write a dot after it to use one of its commands, like snake.move.
explain.game: game is the game itself: the score, game over and speed. Write a dot after it, like game.changeScore.
explain.console: console is the box under your code. console.log writes a message in it.
explain.math: Math has maths helpers, like Math.random() for a random number.
explain.memberUnknown: There is no command called {name}. Look in the Commands list for what {obj} can do.
explain.ownFunction: {name} is the name of a function you made. Use it by writing {name}();
explain.counter: {name} is the loop's counter. It counts 0, 1, 2, … one more each time round the loop.
explain.newVariable: {name} is a new variable: a box with a name that remembers a value.
explain.name: {name} is a name, for example a variable you made. If you meant a command, check the spelling: capital letters matter!
explain.event_click: {name} is a special name: its code runs every time a square is clicked. x and y in the ( ) say which square.
explain.event_rightClick: {name} is a special name: its code runs every time a square is right-clicked.
explain.coord_x: x is the column of the clicked square: 0 is the column on the left. The numbers above the field show the columns.
explain.coord_y: y is the row of the clicked square: 0 is the top row. The numbers left of the field show the rows.
explain.square_x: square.x is the column of the square the loop is visiting right now.
explain.square_y: square.y is the row of the square the loop is visiting right now.
explain.loopItem: {name} is each thing in the list, one at a time: each time round the loop it is the next one.
explain.of: for (… of …) visits every thing in a list, one at a time.
explain.parenForOf: ( ) after for say what to visit: for (const square of list) visits each thing in the list, calling it square.
explain.field: field is the minefield. Write a dot after it to use one of its commands, like field.reveal.
explain.garden: garden is Bit's garden. Write a dot after it to use one of its commands, like garden.build.
explain.item_x: {name}.x is the column of the {name} the loop is visiting right now.
explain.item_y: {name}.y is the row of the {name} the loop is visiting right now.
explain.me: me is the object running this script right now: this bug, or this sprinkler. Every object runs the same script, each with its own me.
explain.me_speed: me.speed is this bug's speed. A bigger number is faster: 0.1 is twice as fast as 0.05.
explain.me_hp: me.hp is this bug's HP: how much water it can take before it is squashed.
explain.me_kind: me.kind is what kind of bug this is: 'snail' or 'beetle'.
explain.me_x: me.x is the column this object is in right now.
explain.me_y: me.y is the row this object is in.
explain.me_move: me.move() moves this bug one small step, as far as its speed says.
explain.me_squash: me.squash() squashes this bug: it is stopped and disappears.
explain.me_shoot: me.shoot() makes this sprinkler shoot a water drop along its row.
explain.event_created: {name} is a special name: its code runs once for each object, the moment it is created.
explain.event_hit: {name} is a special name: its code runs every time water hits this bug.
explain.map: map is the map of the garden. map.put puts grass, a rock or flowers on a square.
explain.gridCounter_x: x is the column counter: the loop runs once for each column, with x = 0, 1, 2 … 8.
explain.gridCounter_y: y is the row counter: the loop runs once for each row, with y = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

glossary.braces: hold a group of code that belongs together: the code of a function, a loop or an if
glossary.parens: after a command: make it run, with extra info inside. After if, for, while: hold the question
glossary.quotes: show where text starts and ends: 'right' is a word, not a command
glossary.semicolon: ends a command, like a full stop
glossary.dot: "belongs to": bit.move is Bit's move command
glossary.assign: puts a value in a variable: let i = 0
glossary.compare: less than and more than: i < 4
glossary.comment: a note for people; the computer skips it
